title: Write a recorded response back as a text block

blocks.text: The team's test generator records what a service returns and writes it into a generated JUnit test as a Java text block, so the next run is compared with exactly that string. Most generated tests work. A few don't compile, and a few fail on the very first run although the service hasn't changed: the string javac reads back from the block isn't the one that was recorded.

`FixtureWriter.textBlock(value)` in `src/main/java/practice/FixtureWriter.java` already writes the delimiters, the indentation and the line breaks between lines. Finish its `TODO`, `line(text)`: what to write for one line of the value so that javac reads that line back exactly. Leave alone whatever needs no change, so the generated fixtures stay readable. Recorded values hold printable ASCII characters, spaces, carriage returns and line feeds.
When you're done, any such value written by `textBlock` compiles, and javac reads it back unchanged. About twelve lines in total.
The tests compile each generated block with the JDK's own compiler and compare the value it holds.

cases.says: a JSON response with quotes and indentation compiles back to the same string
text with blank lines, indented lines and no final line break, and the empty string, compile back unchanged
backslashes, including ones before n, t, d and u and one at the end of a line, compile back as backslashes
three or more quotes in a row, and a quote at the end of the value, compile back unchanged
spaces at the end of a line, and a line of spaces only, survive compilation
a carriage return in the value survives compilation

origin.section: Quotes Need No Escape Until Three Stand in a Row or One Meets the Closing Delimiter

concepts: To write a value back as a text block, escape what would change it: backslashes, runs of three quotes, a space at the end of a line, and a carriage return.
